chunks: And from him, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Abu al-Bakhtari Wahb ibn Wahb al-Qurashi, from Abu Abdillah (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ):

He said: The Commander of the Faithful (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ) said: When a deceased person dies at sea, he is to be washed (ghusl), shrouded, embalmed with hanut, and the funeral prayer (salat) is to be performed over him. Then a stone is tied to his feet and he is cast into the sea.

key_terms.حُنِّطَ: was given hanut — camphor-based preparation applied to the joints and forehead of the deceased
key_terms.صُلِّيَ: the salat al-mayyit (funeral prayer) was performed over him
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: was given ghusl — the ritual washing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia Islamic ruling on performing funeral rites for a person who dies at sea?
ai.summary: Transmitted from Imam al-Sadiq (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ) on the authority of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ), this hadith establishes the complete funeral protocol for a person who dies at sea: all standard rites — ghusl, shrouding, hanut, and salat al-mayyit — must be performed, after which a stone is tied to the feet and the body is committed to the sea. It affirms the Shia jurisprudential principle that normal funeral obligations remain binding even under exceptional circumstances such as death at sea, with sea-burial substituting for ground burial.
